status: PROSPECTIVE SOURCE-ONLY PILOT; implementation preflight required before fitting
authorization: Author authorized continued constructive WACV cross-species research. No further author confirmation required for this source pilot.
question: Can a causal temporal representation shared across neurons learn useful source decoding features beyond matched generic filterbanks, before considering cross-species transfer?
scope: FALCON M1 calibration only; one macaque. No H1, M1 minival, private evaluator or GPU. Source days and fourth-day development have already been examined in earlier experiments; this is exploratory development, not a fresh confirmatory test.

split.order: Four calibration files sorted by date/name
split.checkpoint_and_ridge_selection: Third day REAL neural/EMG windows, identical for all encoders/controls; this real-source supervised selection is disclosed for synthetic/time-trained controls too.
split.window: Reuse L3/L4 exact eligible-row 320-bin prefix and next eight whole query trials, with exact absolute raw-bin IDs saved
split.training_query: First four whole query trials of each sampled training window
split.pairing: Same source window schedule and encoder initialization within seed across real/synthetic/time_shift arms

encoder.shared_unit: Same temporal weights and, for nonlinear variant, biases applied independently to every neuron. No source neuron identities, readout weights or output correspondence transfer.
encoder.input: Raw binned spike counts, causal tap zero at current bin
encoder.reset: Zero history before each trial and file; no future spikes
encoder.initialization: Exact V1 240ms finite exponential plus four causal lags, padded to 25 taps. Same bank initialization for real/synthetic/time_shift. Episode zero is eligible for selection. Nonlinear biases initialize to zero.
encoder.numerical_safeguards: L2 norm of each filter clipped above 2 only (does not alter V1 initialization); fixed smoothness penalty 1e-4 times mean squared adjacent-tap difference; gradient global norm clipped at 1. Same for all arms. Record non-finite losses/updates and skipped updates.
encoder.dimension: 5 times neuron count: 320 on M1; matches V1. No dimension or parameter-count advantage against generic filterbanks.

readout.model: Fresh differentiable closed-form ridge per episode; unpenalized intercept
readout.normalization: Support-only feature mean/std with fixed 0.1 count-unit std floor. Target mean per output and one pooled support scale. Query activity/labels cannot define support normalization or fitted readout.
readout.selection: For each encoder/checkpoint/budget, select ridge on third-day mean window score only; select checkpoint on third-day primary budget320. Each generic baseline receives the same ridge grid. Preserve all selection tables and deterministic tie order.
readout.objective: Query squared error pooled over channels and rows divided by query-label centered sum of squares (variance-weighted R2 loss); global outer gradients explicitly disclosed.
readout.locality: This quality assay uses global supervised outer learning and a closed-form head. It is not a biologically local learner. A local readout would require a later separate experiment.

optimization.synthetic: L3 profile-matched Poisson generator; source EMG labels retained, first-three-day real source profile used. This control carries real source statistics and label-driven temporal autocorrelation; it is not a data-free source.
optimization.time_shift: L3 fixed raw-neural circular time shift per fit day/seed; retain targets, reset encoded features at trial boundaries

comparators.V1: Preserve exact V1 240ms finite exponential and five-lag features; same calibration selection grid. Human V1 lambda1 is not changed or weakened for any later human study.
comparators.sqrt_count_V1: Apply square-root variance stabilization to counts before exact V1 filtering; nonlinearity control
comparators.multiscale: Five hand-designed finite causal exponentials with tau20/60/120/240/480ms, normalized to unit sum and padded to25taps
comparators.random: Three seed-matched banks: Gaussian25tap vectors smoothed by causal three-tap [1,2,1]/4 kernel, truncated25, each rescaled to the V1 initial filter L2 norm; record exact taps. Same dimension and selection grid.

report.score: Float64 variance-weighted R2, all 16 measured EMG outputs, all eligible query rows
report.replicates: Average seeds within window before conditional paired-window bootstrap; display each seed separately. Windows/one animal are not independent animals.
report.artifacts: All checkpoints, source input hashes, window/support/query IDs, selection tables, per-window raw-unit predictions, filter taps/biases/norms, losses and attempted/successful/skipped updates. No failed file/config/seed omitted.
report.interpretation: A source benefit must be distinguished from a cross-species benefit. A failure here does not establish that fixed V1 captures all transferable neural information or that cross-species transfer is impossible.

preflight: Exact linear V1 initialization reproduces V1 raw features and ridge predictions
Finite-difference gradient through shared filter, support normalization and ridge solve in float64
Causality, trial/file reset, no support-query temporal overlap and calibration-only statistics
Neuron permutation equivariance of features and predictions with a correspondingly permuted head
Deterministic paired initialization/window schedule; all arms' source windows and labels match
Changing query labels cannot change fitted support readout; changes outer loss only
No H1 or minival paths accessed; toy and already-seen training calibration smoke only
advance: Complete source pilot and independent audit, then explicitly record research decision. Source quality is an exploratory screen, not a prerequisite proving transfer. No fresh-source or human scores until a separate prospective protocol/decision is recorded. Do not reuse L4 thresholds silently.
